label: Original-phase token from {n,f,k,p,o,x,u,q,d,1} after a t/k/w/v/i earlier in the prefix
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase: 96% of activation mass, never at t=0 or on the delimiter, and very rarely in the copy phase. Rate peaks at original positions 3-6 and is higher on the first occurrence of a token. Activation looks like an additive mix of two things: the current input token (strongest for n and f, then k, p, o, 1, x, d, q, u) and the tokens seen earlier in the prefix (t most of all, then k, w, v, i), with recent tokens (prev and prev2) counting most. The largest activations come from runs like "t t f", "t n", "w t k". The conjunction (current token in the C set AND some t/k/w/v/i earlier) gives dev F1 0.51 and mass recall 0.67. Its misses are other current tokens (e, h, 2) that follow strong history, and its false positives are cases where the history token appeared long ago. Because the contribution is graded rather than clean, no simple boolean predicate gets above about 0.5 F1. Phase restriction alone recovers 96% of the mass but has 14% precision.
